Southeast Alaska Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Juneau AK
301 PM AKDT Fri Oct 23 2026

.SYNOPSIS...

Key Messages:

- Drier trend expected going into the weekend and into next week.

- Clearing skies and cooling trend to start out the weekend, with
  overnight temperatures dipping down into the low to mid 30s, and
  the northern panhandle possibly getting down into the upper 20s.

- Outflow winds become elevated tonight through Saturday as low
  pressure treks south of Haida Gwaii.

&&

.SHORT TERM.../through the weekend/...

A weak surface feature in the central gulf continues to weaken 
and get absorbed into a stronger feature moving south into Haida 
Gwaii through the evening timeframe. To replace this low pressure
in the gulf is a higher amplitude ridge over northern British
Columbia and the Yukon overnight tonight. Between the high
pressure in the Yukon from this ridge, and the stronger low
passing south, northerly winds are expected to strengthen through
the night. Not expecting strong influence from katabatic winds, as
the cold pool in Canada is still relatively warm, hovering around
21 degrees between 925-850 mb. Regardless, land areas exposed to
northerlies, such as Skagway, could see wind gusts as high as 30
mph overnight tonight and into tomorrow. Finally, expect to see
this clearing of skies to last through at least the weekend.

Temperatures are the big headache for this forecast, as with the
clearing skies, radiative cooling could bring temperatures much
lower than expected. For now, temperatures in the Icy Strait
corridor and northern inner channels are hovering near the mid to
upper 20s in sheltered areas, and the low 30s for areas with wind.
Juneau and Petersburg could see some patchy fog overnight, with
Juneau fog, if it develops, likely to deposit as frost rather than
stick around. The same could not be said for Petersburg, as
temperatures are expected to stay above freezing. If widespread
fog does develop going into Saturday, it may stay for much longer
than anticipated from the warming 850 mb temperatures going into
the weekend, strengthening the inversion. 


.LONG TERM.../Monday through Wednesday/...Minimal changes were 
made to the long term forecast as mild weather continues to end 
out the month of October. High pressure remains over the gulf 
through the long term period, with brief interruptions by weak low
pressure systems. The first of these will move across the gulf 
Monday bringing increased cloud cover the the chance for light 
precipitation. The main change with this weak front is that the 
timing looks to have slightly changed with it arriving slightly 
later than initially anticipated. Now arriving Sunday night into 
Monday. Currently no impacts are anticipated with just light 
precipitation expected. The other main change to the long term 
forecast was increasing winds Tuesday as the northerly winds are 
once again likely to increase as the pressure gradient builds. 
Currently strongest winds are most likely to occur over Lynn Canal
into Skagway. 

There is a chance for some northern areas to see slightly below 
average temperatures into next week into the high 20s / low 30s. 
This will be mainly dependent on how clear we get at night, with 
low cloud cover. Otherwise temperatures remain around typical for 
this time of year with maximum temperatures in the 40s and low 
temperatures in the low to mid 30s.

&&

.AVIATION.../Through Saturday afternoon/...
VFR conditions prevail across the panhandle Friday afternoon and
will continue in large part into the upcoming weekend. With 
clearing skies, some patchy fog could develop again overnight into
Saturday in protected areas. Highest confidence would be in the
vicinity of Petersburg and Juneau, though similar to Friday
morning this should notbe particularly thick or long lasting.
Offshore flow aloft and northerly winds at the surface will pick
up gradually into Saturday, though not expecting to be strong
enough to cause any aviation concerns. Strongest winds are
expected to be coming down Lynn Canal and Chatham Strait as well
as out of some interior passes such as Taku Inlet.

&&

.MARINE...
Outer waters: 
A compact low out the Gulf continues to rapidly shift west and
weaken with fresh to strong E-ly winds over the northern Gulf and
outer coastal waters diminishing through the night and turning
more N-ly. Across the southern waters, E-ly winds will increase
and and turn more N-ly through the night into Saturday as a
stronger low pushes south of Haida Gwaii. Winds will become 
strong with seas build 7 to 10 ft. Winds and seas diminish across 
the Gulf and coastal waters Saturday night into Sunday as high 
pressure moves across the Gulf from W to E as the aforementioned 
low departs SE towards Vancouver Island. Winds and seas will 
increase early next week as high pressure builds back into the 
western Gulf and increases the gradient as low pressure develop to
the south, with winds becoming fresh to possibly strong from the 
northwest, especially over the southern waters.

Inside Waters: Increasing offshore winds and seas tonight as
strengthening low pressure moves south of the area. Fresh to 
strong northerly winds and seas 4 to 5 ft through the north/south 
oriented channels through tomorrow as the gradient remains tighter
across the panhandle. Fresh to strong easterly outflow winds 
could also develop across Taku Inlet and Stikine Sound. Winds and 
seas lessen Saturday night into Sunday as the pressure gradient 
turns more parallel to the panhandle as high pressure moving 
across the Gulf and inner channels by Sunday evening. Winds and
seas looks to increase again early next week with as high 
pressure builds back into the northern Gulf and increases the 
gradient as low pressure develops to the south, with
northerly/easterly offshore winds possibly becoming fresh to
strong.

&&
